Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
"David Wilson" <do...@umich.edu> wrote in message news:<j3tBb.196$o32....@news.itd.umich.edu>...


He's referring to the rulebook. The problem is, that such a device is
set up to time each player's turn-time, like in chess, where one
player has a set amount of time to play the game in.

But in Jyhad, every time the acting player plays a card, every other
player on the table has a chance to respond.

So imagine this:

A: "My turn begins." *hits the timer* "I untap. I play a Blood Doll.."
B: "Hang on, give me the timer, I want to counter that with a Sudden
Reversal.."
C: "Wait, I might want to Sudden your Sudden, but I need a minute to
think about it and negotiate with you. Whose time counts down while I
make my decision?"

Either the clock has to pass back and forth between players every time
a card is played (and that can get horribly tedious during a
stealth-vs-intercept scenario), or decks that do a lot of things
during other players turns (wall decks, Madness Network decks, etc)
and very little during their own get a gross advantage that's clearly
not the intent of players having seperate time-to-play in.

-John Flournoy

Messages.Author: Andrew S. Davidson
Messages.Body:
On Sun, 7 Dec 2003 01:04:35 -0800, Kevin M. wrote:

>http://www.123oy.com/g8/Game%20Timer.html
>What do y'all think of the usefulness of this timer for VTES games? Just
>curious. Thanks.

I could have given you a demo at Gencon SoCal as I had one with me.
Next time perhaps.

I've been using the G8 for Shadowfist events. The turns in that game
are similar to those in VTES - the turn belongs mainly to one player
but other players do things too. You can stop the secondary players
from consuming the current player's time by using the pause button but
the interaction would still be too choppy to manage time strictly in
the manner of chess.

My policy is therefore the reverse of chess which has a draconian
penalty for exceeding your ration of time - losing the game if you
don't make a time control. I prefer the carrot to the stick and
reward the fastest player on each table with a small prize like a
booster. This mostly avoids bad-tempered arguments about accurate
timing while still providing an incentive to play quickly. This has
had a major effect upon the play of my girlfriend who is usually a
very deliberate player - thinking through her moves quite carefully
and being maddeningly oblivious to requests to speed up. When the
prize for being quick was instituted, she suddenly became the fastest
player there - greed is good!

The timer is the only one which will support multiplayer games and is
now official equipement for tournament games like Scrabble. It is
well constructed and reasonably cheap - especially if you buy a case
of 8. I recommend it.

The main issue in VTES wouldn't be timing the ordinary play of the
game but would be handling the deal-making and discussion which can
often take many minutes. You could stop the clock for these by using
the pause button but that would be ducking the issue. My opinion is
still that such discussions are illegal unless sanctioned by a game
effect such as the Succubus Club. But, if you allow them, maybe you
could make them manageable by saying that only the current player is
allowed to talk at length - the other players may only make brief
responses such as "Yes" and "No". Then it would be fair for the
discussion time to be charged to the current player.

Andrew
